source.title: Three Cabinet Ministers take oath in Parliament today
source.identity_basis: The official parliament.gov.to subdomain serves the legislative site; its HTML schema identifies the publisher as Legislative Assembly of Tonga and uses the Parliament root as organization/site identity. The title, original path and 18 August 2026 date match the already accepted C01 source listed below.
source.reading_method: Downloaded original HTML retained outside Git; article heading, created/updated dates and every article-body paragraph read. Navigation/share text was separated mechanically with Python standard-library HTMLParser. No source image/likeness review or reuse.
source.whole_body_scope: Eight paragraphs cover the ministers' oaths, three names/portfolios, loyalty to the King, the Acting Speaker welcome and each minister's remarks. No paragraph reports a Crown succession, abdication or death.
source.existing_c01_source_scope: C01 originally used this article only for the acting Speaker claim to_acting_speaker_tuihaangana_20260818. This supplemental C06 review reads the distinct named King wording in paragraph 1.
source.body_identity_limit: The live mail-host response has different bytes from the old archived www/root-host response. It is retained as a new response and never substituted for, or represented as a match to, the historical source pin. The old archive body was not re-retrieved in this pass.
source.post_cutoff_retrieval_limit: The response was retrieved on 1 October 2026. Its event and visible created/updated dates are 18 August 2026; the earlier accepted C01 archive metadata independently records this title/path captured on that same pre-cutoff date.

new_source_observation.reading: The legislature reports that ministers took their oaths that day in service to named King Tupou VI. This is a current named-holder attestation on the article's event date, not an appointment or accession notice.
inferences_not_made: The oath is not a new accession.
The article supplies no reign end.
The three ministers and Acting Speaker are not imported as new holders or made complete terms.

continuity_disposition.recommendation: Accept the historical to_king identity chain through the fixed 2026-09-07 cutoff with this explicit supplemental continuity inference.
basis: The accepted death/devolution evidence already settles the two succession junctions and Tupou VI's 18 March 2012 accession.
The new primary legislature article directly reattests the same named King on 18 August 2026, only 20 calendar days before the cutoff.

The accepted role is a continuing hereditary Crown, not an office that expires at a daily interval or an election-cycle boundary. The legal succession-rule claim to_crown_const2020_succession_c32 supplies institutional context only, not a new historical event.
No contrary Crown death, abdication or succession is identified in the accepted Crown packet or this article. Absence here is not presented as an exhaustive search of every possible record.

A review can reasonably carry this continuing incumbent across the short remainder without demanding one attestation per day; the extension is recorded as review inference, not attributed to explicit wording of the article.
limits: This recommendation concerns historical identity-chain continuity, not constitutional/legal adjudication.
It grants no post-cutoff replacement or heir accession.
A subsequently discovered contradictory primary source would reopen the affected interval.
Date-boundary/save/production and future institutional succession validation must retain their independently evidenced status. Country completion and human sign-off are not awarded here.
